questions.q: What does RIGHT JOIN keep, compared to LEFT JOIN?
options: Every row from the table on the right side of JOIN, matched or not
Every row from the table on the left side of JOIN, matched or not
Only rows that match on both sides, same as INNER JOIN
Only rows with no match on either side
questions.explain: RIGHT JOIN is the mirror image of LEFT JOIN — it guarantees every row from the right-hand table appears.

questions.q: Can every RIGHT JOIN be rewritten as an equivalent LEFT JOIN?
options: Yes — by swapping which table is named first in the FROM/JOIN order
No, RIGHT JOIN produces results LEFT JOIN can never replicate
Only if the tables have no foreign key relationship
Only when using an INNER JOIN instead
questions.explain: Swapping table order and switching RIGHT JOIN to LEFT JOIN produces an identical result set.

questions.q: Why does this course always use LEFT JOIN instead of RIGHT JOIN?
options: For consistency — it's easier to track 'the table that must appear' when it's always named first
Because RIGHT JOIN is deprecated in SQL Server
Because RIGHT JOIN cannot be combined with WHERE
Because RIGHT JOIN only works with two tables, never three or more
questions.explain: RIGHT JOIN isn't broken — it's a style/readability preference, especially valuable once queries join several tables.

questions.q: In 'FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS sod RIGHT JOIN Production.Product AS p ON sod.ProductID = p.ProductID', which table's unmatched rows get NULL-filled?
options: SalesOrderDetail's columns (the left table) get NULL-filled for products with no orders
Product's columns get NULL-filled
Neither table's columns are ever NULL-filled in a RIGHT JOIN
Both tables' columns are always NULL-filled
questions.explain: Since Product is the right table (kept in full), any product without a matching order gets NULLs in SalesOrderDetail's columns — the left table.

questions.q: Should you still recognize RIGHT JOIN even if you never write it yourself?
options: Yes — you'll encounter it in other people's code even if this course prefers LEFT JOIN
No, it's obsolete and never appears in real code
Only database administrators need to know RIGHT JOIN
RIGHT JOIN and LEFT JOIN have completely different use cases with no overlap
questions.explain: RIGHT JOIN is valid, standard T-SQL — this course's LEFT JOIN preference is a style choice, not a claim that RIGHT JOIN is wrong.
